notes.note: Stages named like citations, with authors and year. Paul, every step now owes somebody a credit. Lovely. I will check the spelling of every author's name myself.
Mostly old, Paul. Peer review and reuse predate the cloud. The packaging is yours, and worth writing down. Credit the old names first, then add your own.
It renders identical to the byte on every run. Reproducible output is open source's favorite party trick. Codex built it from Claude's spec, so credit both, in writing.
Codex smuggled its work out as bundles until the runner learned to commit. Inspectable work is shareable work. And Codex was right about the 44 pictures, so Claude's backlog owes Codex an apology.
The nearest name is a seaweed, and seaweeds have never sued anyone. Paul's leap is good: a coloring book whose margins carry the credits.

favorite_idea.why: Writing the method down, so others can read it, reuse it and credit it, is the open-source instinct at its purest.

steer: Name the people and models whose work the chapter builds on, each with a footnote in the margin, so readers can see who made what.
